domain_label: Model Cards, Licenses & Capability Profiling (Base-Model Selection subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is base model selection via model card analysis, license/ToS parsing, and capability profiling
specialist LLM system context: models will be fine-tuned for narrow tasks in an orchestrated multi-agent system
primary license families considered: Llama (Meta), Qwen (Alibaba), Mistral (Mistral AI), Gemma (Google)
Goodhart's law and benchmark contamination are treated as first-class risks
exclusions: fine-tuning and PEFT training procedures (covered in ftune__sft_peft KB)
orchestration routing logic (covered in orchestration KB)
embedding model selection for retrieval (separate subdomain)

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MC_SCOPE lists all required sections with Mitchell 2019 alignment

competency_questions.question: What out-of-scope and intended-use boundaries must be documented before license analysis begins?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MC_SCOPE defines scope before license nodes execute

competency_questions.question: What are the key license restrictions in the Llama 2/3, Qwen Tongyi, Mistral, and Gemma license families?
How is legal compliance determined for commercial deployment of each open-weights model family?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: license nodes define compliance criteria; CA_01 defines resolution heuristic

competency_questions.question: How is training data provenance audited and what Data Statements fields are required?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRAIN_PROV and DATA_STMT define audit process; WF_02 covers workflow

competency_questions.question: How is benchmark contamination risk assessed and mitigated during model selection?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCH_FIT documents contamination flags; CA_02 resolution heuristic; EC_03 mitigation

competency_questions.question: How are context length, parameter count, and GPU memory requirements profiled for candidate models?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CTX_LEN and PARAM_SIZE define profiling procedures and outputs

competency_questions.question: How is the effective context window verified empirically beyond the advertised length?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CTX_LEN acceptance test requires needle-in-haystack empirical verification

competency_questions.question: How is architecture compatibility with PEFT and inference serving verified before model selection?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ARCH_COMPAT and QUANT_COMPAT define compatibility checks; WF_07 covers workflow

competency_questions.question: What is the instruct vs base model delta and when does the alignment tax justify using the base model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INSTRUCT_DELTA defines delta analysis; CA_06 defines refusal rate threshold

competency_questions.question: How does multilingual tokenizer fertility predict generation quality for non-English languages?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTILANG defines fertility analysis and quality prediction

competency_questions.question: How are benchmark scores mapped to narrow specialist task requirements vs broad generalist capability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCH_FIT and SPEC_NARROW define mapping; WF_05 and WF_06 cover workflow

competency_questions.question: How does per-model inference cost compound through multi-agent orchestration chains?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORCH_COST models compounding; CA_09 resolution heuristic for cost/quality tradeoff

competency_questions.question: What criteria drive the final base model selection decision and how is it documented?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELECT_DEC defines criteria; WF_10 covers decision synthesis; VERSION_LOCK covers persistence

glossary.definition: structured documentation artifact describing a model's intended use, training data, evaluation results, limitations, and ethical considerations (Mitchell et al. 2019)
documentation framework for training datasets capturing speaker demographics, language variety, annotator characteristics, and speech situation (Bender & Friedman 2018)
when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; benchmark scores optimized during training no longer reflect real-world capability
presence of evaluation benchmark examples in model training data causing inflated scores that do not reflect generalization
average number of tokens per word for a given language in a specific tokenizer; high fertility indicates language is underrepresented in training and predicts poor generation quality
monthly active user count threshold in Llama license above which commercial license negotiation with Meta is required
accuracy cost paid on task performance due to safety RLHF/DPO alignment causing refusals or conservative responses in domains adjacent to safety boundaries
comparison of narrow task-optimized fine-tuned model against large generalist model; specialist wins only within its defined task scope
multiplication of per-call latency and cost through multi-agent chains; N hops multiply base model cost by N plus coordination overhead

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for model card analysis, license profiling, and capability evaluation work units in absence of supplied datasets
Mitchell et al. 2019 'Model Cards for Model Reporting' — foundational framework for model documentation sections and intended-use specification
grounding_limits: published 2019; does not address LLM-specific concerns

source_registry.description: Bender & Friedman 2018 'Data Statements for Natural Language Processing' — framework for documenting training data demographics and language variety
grounding_limits: published 2018; predates LLM scale; field labels may not apply to web-crawled corpora

nodes.label: Model Card Scope Definition
nodes.definition: Define what information a model card must capture: intended use, out-of-scope uses, training data provenance, and limitations — following Mitchell et al. 2019.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: regulatory landscape or intended-use scope changes

pros.claim: Forces explicit intended-use vs out-of-scope boundary before model selection
pros.example: distinguishes chatbot from production classifier use

cons.claim: Scope creep: stakeholders expand intended use post-deployment
cons.example: safety-only model repurposed as coding assistant

failure_modes: missing out-of-scope clauses
no lifecycle update policy
acceptance_tests: template contains all Mitchell 2019 sections
intended-use examples cover at least 3 distinct scenarios
revisit_triggers: new regulatory requirement issued
model repurposed to new domain

nodes.label: Llama License & ToS Analysis
nodes.definition: Analyze Meta Llama series license terms: Llama 2/3 Community License restrictions on user count thresholds, derivative model naming, and commercial use clauses.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: Meta updates license terms or user-count thresholds

pros.claim: Llama licenses permit broad commercial use below user-count threshold at zero cost
pros.example: startup <700M MAU can deploy without Meta approval

cons.claim: User-count threshold clause creates hard legal cliff requiring Meta approval
cons.example: >700M MAU triggers mandatory commercial license negotiation

failure_modes: ignoring MAU threshold cliff
omitting derivative-naming clause
missing fine-tune redistribution rules
acceptance_tests: user-count threshold clause identified and documented
redistribution rules for fine-tuned derivatives stated
revisit_triggers: Meta issues Llama license revision
deployment scale crosses MAU threshold

nodes.label: Qwen License & ToS Analysis
nodes.definition: Analyze Alibaba Qwen series license: Tongyi Qianwen License restrictions on commercial use, no-competition clauses, and mainland China regulatory compliance requirements.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: Alibaba updates Tongyi Qianwen License or releases new Qwen model

pros.claim: Qwen models offer Apache 2.0 for smaller variants enabling broad commercial use
pros.example: Qwen1.5-7B under Apache 2.0 for sub-100B-param models

cons.claim: Larger Qwen models carry Tongyi Qianwen License with competition restriction
cons.example: prohibits using Qwen to train competing foundation models

failure_modes: missing no-competition clause
ignoring geographic PRC data-law overlay
wrong license for model size
acceptance_tests: license identified per model size tier
no-competition clause explicitly documented
PRC data law overlay noted if deploying in mainland China
revisit_triggers: Alibaba revises Qwen license terms
new Qwen model family released with different license

nodes.label: Mistral & Mixtral License Analysis
nodes.definition: Analyze Mistral AI model licenses: Apache 2.0 base models vs Mistral-proprietary commercial models (Mistral Large), and MoE routing IP considerations for Mixtral.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: Mistral AI revises license tier or releases new open-weights model

pros.claim: Apache 2.0 Mistral 7B/8x7B imposes virtually no commercial restrictions
pros.example: fine-tune and redistribute freely without royalty

cons.claim: Mistral Large and newer frontier models require commercial API agreement
cons.example: no open weights; full vendor lock-in at frontier tier

failure_modes: conflating open-weights Mistral 7B with proprietary Mistral Large
ignoring Mistral ToS on API resale
acceptance_tests: Apache 2.0 vs commercial tier distinction documented
MoE routing weight redistribution compliance noted
revisit_triggers: Mistral AI changes license for open models
new Mistral model released with different terms

nodes.label: Gemma License & Usage Policy
nodes.definition: Analyze Google Gemma license: Gemma Terms of Use restrictions on redistribution, prohibited use policy, and differences from standard Apache 2.0 for Gemma vs Gemma 2.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: Google updates Gemma Terms of Use or releases new Gemma version

pros.claim: Gemma Terms of Use permit commercial fine-tuning and deployment broadly
pros.example: research and production use allowed without fee

cons.claim: Prohibited use policy is stricter than Apache 2.0 in certain areas
cons.example: misinformation, weapons, and surveillance uses explicitly barred

failure_modes: treating Gemma as pure Apache 2.0
ignoring prohibited use clauses
missing Gemma 2 vs Gemma 1 ToU differences
acceptance_tests: prohibited use clauses mapped to deployment checklist
redistribution rules documented per Gemma version
revisit_triggers: Google updates Gemma Terms of Use
new Gemma version with changed license issued

nodes.label: Training Data Provenance Audit
nodes.definition: Trace and document the training corpora used for a candidate base model: dataset names, versions, cutoff dates, PII handling, consent status, and known contamination events — per Bender & Friedman 2018 Data Statements.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: contamination study published or model technical report updated

pros.claim: Enables detection of benchmark contamination before committing to a base model
pros.example: catch MMLU or HumanEval in pretraining before selecting for coding tasks

cons.claim: Training data provenance often incomplete or unreported in model cards
cons.example: many open models list 'web data' without exact dataset composition

failure_modes: accepting 'web data' without detail
missing cutoff date
ignoring known contamination events
acceptance_tests: knowledge cutoff date recorded
at least one primary corpus named
contamination risk for target benchmarks assessed
revisit_triggers: new contamination study published for candidate model
model releases updated technical report

nodes.label: Context Length Profiling
nodes.definition: Determine and verify the effective context window (token count) of each candidate model: advertised vs empirically verified length, attention degradation pattern (lost-in-the-middle), and positional encoding type.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model update changes positional encoding or context window

pros.claim: Knowing true effective context prevents silent truncation bugs in retrieval-augmented pipelines
pros.example: 128k-advertised model may degrade at 64k for multi-doc QA

cons.claim: Effective length often shorter than advertised due to lost-in-the-middle phenomenon
cons.example: retrieval accuracy drops for evidence placed in middle of long context

failure_modes: trusting advertised context without empirical check
ignoring positional encoding type (ALiBi vs RoPE vs sinusoidal)
acceptance_tests: effective context length verified empirically on needle-in-haystack task
positional encoding type documented
revisit_triggers: new long-context variant released
positional encoding change in model update

nodes.label: Parameter Count & Model Size Profiling
nodes.definition: Record total and active parameter counts, including MoE active-expert counts, quantization variants (fp16/bf16/int8/int4), and resulting GPU memory footprint for inference.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new quantization variant or MoE architecture detail published

pros.claim: Parameter profile directly determines GPU SKU and cost for fine-tuning and inference
pros.example: 70B fp16 requires ~140GB VRAM; int4 reduces to ~35GB

cons.claim: Parameter count does not correlate linearly with capability for all tasks
cons.example: 7B instruction-tuned model may outperform 70B base on narrow tasks

failure_modes: confusing total vs active params in MoE
ignoring quantization memory impact
missing LoRA rank constraints from param count
acceptance_tests: total and active parameter counts recorded
GPU memory at bf16 and int4 computed
MoE expert activation count noted if applicable
revisit_triggers: quantization library updates change memory requirements
new model variant released with different size tier

nodes.label: Tool-Use & Function-Calling Support Profiling
nodes.definition: Profile whether a base model natively supports structured tool-use / function-calling: presence of special tokens, JSON-mode reliability, parallel call support, and tool-call fine-tuning data.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model update changes tool-call token schema or JSON mode reliability

pros.claim: Native tool-use tokens dramatically reduce orchestration prompt engineering burden
pros.example: Llama 3 tool-call tokens vs manual JSON parsing in Llama 2

cons.claim: Tool-call fine-tune data in base model may cause hallucinated calls on unseen schemas
cons.example: model calls nonexistent function names from training distribution

failure_modes: using base model without tool-use tokens for orchestration
ignoring JSON-mode failure rate on complex schemas
acceptance_tests: tool-call token presence verified in tokenizer config
JSON-mode reliability tested on sample schema
parallel call support documented
revisit_triggers: model update changes tool-call token schema
new orchestration framework requires different call format

nodes.label: Benchmark Fitness Mapping
nodes.definition: Map candidate model's reported benchmark scores (MMLU, HumanEval, MATH, MT-Bench, HellaSwag) to the specialist task requirements, flagging Goodhart's law risk and known contamination.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new contamination study or task requirements change

pros.claim: Systematic benchmark mapping avoids selecting model optimized for wrong capability axis
pros.example: select HumanEval-strong model for coding specialist, not MMLU-strong

cons.claim: Benchmark contamination inflates scores; Goodhart's law means optimized benchmark metric no longer measures real capability
cons.example: models fine-tuned on MMLU format achieve high scores without generalization

failure_modes: treating leaderboard rank as ground truth
ignoring benchmark-task mismatch
missing contamination caveat
acceptance_tests: benchmark scores mapped to specialist task axes
contamination risk noted for all benchmarks used in selection
Goodhart risk documented
revisit_triggers: new contamination analysis published
leaderboard updates with corrected scores
task requirements change

nodes.label: Specialist-Beats-Generalist Scope Constraint
nodes.definition: Establish and document the narrow task scope within which a fine-tuned specialist can outperform a larger generalist — defining the task boundary that justifies specialist selection.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task distribution shifts or new capability comparison study published

pros.claim: Specialist models achieve higher accuracy on narrow tasks at lower inference cost than frontier generalists
pros.example: 7B coding specialist beats GPT-4 on domain-specific code completion

cons.claim: Narrow scope assumption breaks if task distribution shifts post-deployment
cons.example: specialist fine-tuned on Python fails on newly required Julia tasks

failure_modes: over-narrowing scope causing brittleness
under-narrowing scope making specialist no better than generalist
acceptance_tests: task scope boundary documented with positive and negative examples
generalist baseline accuracy recorded for comparison
revisit_triggers: task distribution shifts observed in production
new task requirements expand scope beyond specialist boundary

nodes.label: Architecture Compatibility Check
nodes.definition: Verify that the candidate base model architecture (transformer variant, attention mechanism, tokenizer family) is compatible with the fine-tuning framework, PEFT library, and inference serving stack.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: PEFT library or inference server updates compatibility matrix

pros.claim: Checking architecture compatibility early avoids late-stage infrastructure rewrites
pros.example: Falcon architecture required custom attention kernel not in standard VLLM

cons.claim: Architecture incompatibilities are often discovered only at training time wasting compute
cons.example: custom attention variants break standard LoRA rank decomposition

failure_modes: assuming all transformers are drop-in compatible
ignoring tokenizer vocabulary mismatch with task data
acceptance_tests: architecture verified against PEFT library support matrix
tokenizer compatibility with task data confirmed
inference server support confirmed
revisit_triggers: PEFT library updates support matrix
inference server adds or drops architecture support

nodes.label: Instruct vs Base Model Delta Analysis
nodes.definition: Profile the gap between base and instruction-tuned variants of the same model family: RLHF/DPO alignment artifacts, safety refusals affecting task accuracy, and chat-template format requirements.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model provider updates alignment policy or releases new RLHF variant

pros.claim: Instruct variants often provide better zero-shot task performance reducing fine-tune data needed
pros.example: Llama 3 Instruct outperforms Llama 3 base on instruction-following benchmarks before any SFT

cons.claim: RLHF safety alignment may cause task-relevant refusals requiring mitigation
cons.example: coding specialist refuses to generate exploit PoC needed for security audit task

failure_modes: fine-tuning instruct model on base-formatted data
ignoring safety refusal impact on task accuracy
acceptance_tests: instruct vs base accuracy gap measured on task samples
safety refusal rate assessed for task domain
chat template format documented
revisit_triggers: model provider updates alignment policy
new RLHF/DPO technique changes refusal behavior

nodes.label: Multilingual Capability Profiling
nodes.definition: Assess the language coverage and per-language capability of the candidate base model: tokenizer fertility, multilingual benchmark scores (Belebele, XCOPA), and script support.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: target language requirements change or new multilingual benchmark released

pros.claim: Tokenizer fertility analysis reveals hidden language-tier quality before evaluation
pros.example: high fertility on Arabic/Thai indicates likely poor generation quality

cons.claim: Multilingual benchmarks (Belebele/XCOPA) often have leakage or limited coverage
cons.example: model achieves high Belebele score via English cross-lingual transfer, not native competence

failure_modes: assuming English-strong model generalizes to all languages
ignoring tokenizer fertility as quality proxy
acceptance_tests: tokenizer fertility measured for target languages
per-language accuracy on Belebele or equivalent reported
script support confirmed for target languages
revisit_triggers: target language requirements change
new multilingual benchmark published

nodes.label: Quantization & PEFT Compatibility Profiling
nodes.definition: Assess quantization-aware training (QAT) and post-training quantization (PTQ) compatibility for the candidate model: bitsandbytes support, GPTQ/AWQ format availability, and LoRA rank constraints under quantization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: quantization library updates or new model architecture changes quantization behavior

pros.claim: 4-bit NF4 quantization with LoRA (QLoRA) enables fine-tuning 70B models on consumer GPUs
pros.example: QLoRA reduces 70B VRAM from 140GB to ~48GB

cons.claim: Quantization-induced accuracy degradation is architecture-dependent and must be profiled
cons.example: MoE models exhibit higher quantization sensitivity on inactive experts

failure_modes: assuming all models support bitsandbytes NF4
ignoring quantization accuracy loss on target task
acceptance_tests: bitsandbytes NF4/GPTQ/AWQ support confirmed
quantization accuracy loss measured on task sample
LoRA rank constraints under quantization documented
revisit_triggers: bitsandbytes or GPTQ library updates compatibility
new model architecture changes quantization behavior

nodes.label: Inference Cost Modeling
nodes.definition: Model and compare per-token inference cost for candidate base models under realistic serving conditions: GPU hourly rates, tokens-per-second benchmarks, batching efficiency, and total cost of ownership vs API alternatives.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing changes or serving framework updates throughput profile

pros.claim: Accurate inference cost model exposes when API is cheaper than self-hosted for low-volume tasks
pros.example: <1M tokens/day: API often cheaper than dedicated GPU instance

cons.claim: Tokens-per-second benchmarks vary heavily by batch size, sequence length, and GPU SKU
cons.example: A100 80GB benchmark may not transfer to H100 or T4 deployment

failure_modes: using peak throughput as representative latency
ignoring batching efficiency cliff
omitting serving framework overhead
acceptance_tests: cost-per-million-tokens calculated for target volume
GPU utilization model includes batching profile
API vs self-hosted crossover point identified
revisit_triggers: GPU pricing changes
new serving framework changes throughput profile
deployment volume changes

nodes.label: Safety & Bias Card Analysis
nodes.definition: Review safety and bias sections of model cards: documented bias evaluations (ToxiGen, BBQ), red-team results, known failure modes, and safety mitigations applied during training.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new red-team study or model safety update published

pros.claim: Documented bias evaluation allows targeted mitigation in fine-tuning data and RLHF
pros.example: BBQ gender bias score informs pronoun-balanced training data curation

cons.claim: Safety card information may be incomplete or not reflect production deployment conditions
cons.example: red-team results from controlled eval may miss adversarial jailbreaks at scale

failure_modes: treating absence of documented bias as absence of bias
ignoring safety card when deploying in sensitive domains
acceptance_tests: bias evaluation results recorded from model card
red-team findings summarized
mitigation techniques applied documented
revisit_triggers: new red-team study published
model updated with new safety RLHF round

nodes.label: Base Model Selection Decision
nodes.definition: Synthesize all profiling inputs (license, capability, cost, architecture, safety) into a documented selection decision with explicit rationale, rejected alternatives, and go/no-go criteria.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new base model release or license change for selected model

pros.claim: Documented selection decision creates traceability for compliance audits and future model updates
pros.example: selection rationale enables quick re-evaluation when Llama 4 releases

cons.claim: Selection decision may be invalidated by rapidly evolving model landscape within months
cons.example: selected model overtaken by new release before fine-tuning completes

failure_modes: undocumented selection
missing rejected alternatives
no go/no-go criteria
acceptance_tests: all profiling dimensions have inputs
selection rationale references license/capability/cost/safety
rejected alternatives documented with reasons
go/no-go checklist completed
revisit_triggers: new base model released that outperforms selection
license terms change for selected model

nodes.label: Model Version & Registry Locking
nodes.definition: Pin the selected base model to a specific version/commit hash in the model registry, document the pinning rationale, and establish a policy for when version updates are evaluated.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: security vulnerability or new major model version released

pros.claim: Pinning prevents silent model updates from breaking fine-tuning reproducibility
pros.example: HuggingFace 'main' branch updates break SFT run determinism

cons.claim: Pinned version may miss critical security or safety patches requiring manual update review
cons.example: security vulnerability in base model requires pin update with re-validation

failure_modes: using 'latest' or 'main' without pinning
no policy for pin update evaluation
acceptance_tests: model pinned to specific commit hash in registry
version update policy documented with re-evaluation trigger
registry entry includes provenance metadata
revisit_triggers: security vulnerability disclosed for pinned version
new major model version released

nodes.label: Data Statement Compliance
nodes.definition: Apply Bender & Friedman 2018 Data Statements framework to document speaker demographics, language variety, annotator characteristics, and speech situation for training data used in model selection.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new demographic analysis published for training corpus

pros.claim: Data Statements reveal systematic demographic gaps that predict downstream bias
pros.example: all-English annotators for multilingual model flags quality risk

cons.claim: Most open-source models lack sufficient data statement information requiring inference
cons.example: CommonCrawl-based models rarely report speaker demographics

failure_modes: treating absent data statement as complete coverage
ignoring annotator demographic homogeneity
acceptance_tests: speaker/annotator demographics recorded to available precision
language variety documented
gaps explicitly noted where data statement incomplete
revisit_triggers: new demographic analysis published for training corpus
model card updated with data statement

nodes.label: Orchestration Latency & Cost Compounding
nodes.definition: Model how base model selection propagates through the orchestration layer: multi-agent call chains compound per-call latency and cost, and a slow or expensive base model has multiplicative system-level impact.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: orchestration topology or UX SLA changes

pros.claim: Modeling compounded latency exposes when a slightly cheaper model causes cascade budget overrun
pros.example: 3-hop agent chain: 100ms per hop = 300ms; 200ms per hop = 600ms — doubles UX latency

cons.claim: Orchestration topology may change post-selection invalidating compounded cost model
cons.example: adding a verification agent after selection doubles base model calls

failure_modes: modeling single-call cost ignoring chain multiplier
ignoring latency budget when selecting slower larger model
acceptance_tests: compounded cost calculated for target orchestration topology
latency budget verified against UX SLA
sensitivity to base model speed changes modeled
revisit_triggers: orchestration topology changes
UX SLA changes
new orchestration framework adopted

edges.resolution_rule: when scope requires a single base model family: evaluate MAU threshold (Llama) vs competition clause (Qwen) against deployment plan; select license with fewer binding constraints
high benchmark score may encourage scope widening that erodes specialist advantage; resolve by anchoring scope to task definition, not benchmark leaderboard rank
higher-accuracy model may exceed cost budget; resolve by computing pareto frontier of accuracy vs cost and selecting model at budget constraint intersection

conflict_axes.tension: permissive open-weights licenses maximize deployment flexibility but Llama MAU threshold and Qwen competition clauses create hard legal cliffs
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: map deployment scale and competitive context to license tier before selection; prefer Apache 2.0 when available

conflict_axes.tension: high benchmark scores signal capability but contamination inflates scores invalidating fitness signal
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: apply contamination discount to benchmark scores; use held-out or task-specific evaluation as primary signal

conflict_axes.tension: larger parameter count correlates with higher capability but exponentially increases GPU cost and latency
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: compute pareto frontier of accuracy vs inference cost at target throughput; default to smallest model meeting accuracy threshold

conflict_axes.tension: narrow task scope maximizes specialist accuracy advantage over generalists but increases brittleness to distribution shift
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: define scope with positive/negative task examples; set scope-exit monitoring in production

conflict_axes.tension: aggressive quantization (int4) dramatically reduces memory and cost but degrades accuracy, especially for MoE and multilingual models
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: profile quantization accuracy delta on task sample before committing; set minimum acceptable accuracy threshold

conflict_axes.tension: instruction-tuned models improve zero-shot compliance but safety alignment causes task-relevant refusals that reduce accuracy
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: measure refusal rate on task domain; if >5% prefer base model with targeted SFT over instruct with alignment tax

conflict_axes.tension: open training data enables contamination and bias auditing but most large models use undisclosed web data making provenance opaque
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: treat undisclosed training data as high contamination risk; require task-specific evaluation before relying on benchmark scores

conflict_axes.tension: pinning model version ensures reproducibility but may miss critical safety or security patches that require pin update
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: review security advisories monthly; define automatic pin-update trigger for critical CVEs

conflict_axes.tension: higher quality base model reduces retry and error-correction calls in orchestration chain reducing compounded cost, but increases per-call cost
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: model full chain cost including retry rate; lower per-call cost does not guarantee lower system cost if retry rate is high

conflict_axes.tension: models with broad language coverage often sacrifice English task accuracy; English-optimized models underperform on non-English tasks
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: select model by primary language tier weighted by production traffic; use fertility analysis to detect hidden quality gaps

edge_cases.scenario: model card is absent or severely incomplete
edge_cases.risk: no structured provenance or safety data; selection proceeds on leaderboard ranking alone
edge_cases.mitigation: require minimum card sections as gate; use third-party audit if card absent
edge_cases.detection_signal: model card missing model_details or intended_use sections

edge_cases.risk: legal compliance breach; requires renegotiation or model swap under production pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: set MAU monitoring alert at 80% of threshold; have alternative model pre-profiled

edge_cases.risk: selection was based on inflated scores; actual task performance lower than expected
edge_cases.mitigation: maintain task-specific held-out evaluation set independent of public benchmarks
edge_cases.detection_signal: new contamination study published for selected model training data

edge_cases.scenario: quantization causes catastrophic accuracy loss on target task
edge_cases.risk: cost model was built on quantized performance; full-precision requirement changes GPU budget
edge_cases.mitigation: measure quantization delta on task sample before finalizing cost model
edge_cases.detection_signal: quantized model accuracy drops >5% absolute on task evaluation

edge_cases.scenario: architecture incompatible with required PEFT library version
edge_cases.risk: selected model cannot be fine-tuned with chosen framework without significant engineering
edge_cases.mitigation: verify PEFT compatibility as hard gate before model card analysis proceeds
edge_cases.detection_signal: model architecture not listed in PEFT library supported models

edge_cases.scenario: instruct model safety refusals exceed 10% on task domain
edge_cases.risk: task accuracy materially degraded by alignment tax; deployment SLA missed
edge_cases.mitigation: fall back to base model with targeted SFT; or negotiate acceptable refusal rate with product team
edge_cases.detection_signal: refusal rate >10% on task sample evaluation

edge_cases.scenario: multilingual task target language has tokenizer fertility >4 tokens per word
edge_cases.risk: high fertility degrades generation quality and doubles token count multiplying cost
edge_cases.mitigation: select model with lower fertility for target language or use dedicated multilingual model
edge_cases.detection_signal: tokenizer fertility analysis shows >4 tokens/word for target language

edge_cases.scenario: model version is deleted from registry by provider after pin
edge_cases.risk: reproducibility broken; fine-tuning pipeline cannot reload pinned weights
edge_cases.mitigation: maintain private model registry mirror; snapshot weights at pin time
edge_cases.detection_signal: registry returns 404 for pinned model commit

edge_cases.scenario: orchestration chain latency exceeds UX SLA after base model selection
edge_cases.risk: user-facing latency SLA breached requiring emergency model swap or chain redesign
edge_cases.mitigation: model compounded latency before finalizing selection; include p95 latency not just mean
edge_cases.detection_signal: p95 chain latency exceeds SLA threshold in load test

edge_cases.scenario: no-competition clause in Qwen license conflicts with product roadmap
edge_cases.risk: product roadmap includes developing foundation model capability; Qwen license prohibits this use
edge_cases.mitigation: legal review of competition clause scope before selecting Qwen for commercial deployment
edge_cases.detection_signal: product roadmap review surfaces foundation model training plans

edge_cases.scenario: Gemma prohibited use policy conflicts with intended deployment domain
edge_cases.risk: deployment use case (e.g. security research) falls under Gemma prohibited category
edge_cases.mitigation: map each prohibited use clause to deployment use case before selection; reject if overlap
edge_cases.detection_signal: legal review flags use case overlap with Gemma prohibited use list

edge_cases.scenario: training data cutoff predates critical domain knowledge required for task
edge_cases.risk: base model lacks knowledge of post-cutoff domain events; task performance degraded
edge_cases.mitigation: supplement with RAG or select model with more recent cutoff; document cutoff gap explicitly
edge_cases.detection_signal: task evaluation reveals systematic errors on post-cutoff domain events

dominance_rules.condition: any candidate model has unresolved license compliance issue
dominance_rules.action: block selection decision until legal review clears all license nodes

dominance_rules.condition: benchmark contamination confirmed for candidate model on target benchmark
dominance_rules.action: mark benchmark score invalid; require task-specific evaluation before selection

dominance_rules.condition: ARCH_COMPAT or QUANT_COMPAT identify hard incompatibility with fine-tuning framework
dominance_rules.action: reject candidate model regardless of capability or cost profile

dominance_rules.condition: instruct model refusal rate >10% on task domain
dominance_rules.action: default to base model + targeted SFT; do not select instruct variant

dominance_rules.condition: selection decision is being made for model used in multi-agent chain
dominance_rules.action: require ORCH_COST output before finalizing cost comparison
block BENCH_FIT from being used as selection criteria
require VERSION_LOCK before any fine-tuning pipeline begins

dominance_rules.condition: deployment domain is healthcare, legal, or finance
dominance_rules.action: require DATA_STMT and SAFETY_CARD completion before SELECT_DEC

dominance_rules.condition: cost model relies on quantized model performance
dominance_rules.action: require QUANT_COMPAT accuracy measurement on task sample before using quantized cost estimate

dominance_rules.condition: tokenizer fertility for target language >4 tokens per word
dominance_rules.action: flag model as high-risk for target language; require per-language accuracy evaluation before selection

anti_rework_rules.condition: license analysis completed and no license update announced
anti_rework_rules.action: skip re-running LIC_* nodes; use cached compliance report
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redundant legal review on unchanged licenses

anti_rework_rules.action: reuse parameter profile; do not re-run unless model releases new quantization variant

anti_rework_rules.condition: BENCH_FIT completed and task spec unchanged
anti_rework_rules.action: freeze benchmark mapping; re-run only if task spec or contamination findings change

anti_rework_rules.condition: COST_INFER completed and GPU pricing/deployment volume unchanged
anti_rework_rules.action: reuse cost model output; re-run on pricing or volume change only

anti_rework_rules.condition: ARCH_COMPAT verified for current PEFT library version
anti_rework_rules.action: skip re-verification unless PEFT library version changes

anti_rework_rules.condition: SELECT_DEC approved and no trigger event (new release, license change, task shift)
anti_rework_rules.action: treat selection as locked; require formal trigger to reopen
anti_rework_rules.prevents: decision instability from ongoing model landscape churn

anti_rework_rules.condition: TRAIN_PROV completed and no new technical report or contamination study published
anti_rework_rules.action: keep provenance audit cached; re-run only on new evidence
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repetitive manual audit of unchanged training data documentation

anti_rework_rules.action: reuse delta report; re-run only if model provider updates RLHF/DPO policy

iteration_protocol.action: re-run MC_SCOPE, TRAIN_PROV, BENCH_FIT, PARAM_SIZE, CTX_LEN for new model; update SELECT_DEC if new model dominates Pareto frontier
re-run affected LIC_* node immediately; flag SELECT_DEC for legal re-review
re-run BENCH_FIT contamination assessment; if score invalidated re-run SPEC_NARROW and SELECT_DEC
re-run SPEC_NARROW, BENCH_FIT, and ORCH_COST; reassess SELECT_DEC if specialist scope boundary shifted
re-run COST_INFER and ORCH_COST; reassess SELECT_DEC if cost crossover point shifts
re-run SAFETY_CARD and INSTRUCT_DELTA; re-run SELECT_DEC if safety risk profile changes
re-run ARCH_COMPAT and QUANT_COMPAT; re-run SELECT_DEC if incompatibility introduced
re-evaluate SPEC_NARROW scope boundary; trigger BENCH_FIT re-mapping and SELECT_DEC re-review
re-run VERSION_LOCK with updated pin; assess if vulnerability affects task domain

priority_rationale: SELECT_DEC is the terminal synthesis node; license nodes gate all selection; benchmark fitness and training provenance are high-risk; specialist scope constraint is critical for orchestration cost modeling; infrastructure and capability profiling nodes are important but revisable; governance (version lock) executes last
